Samsung reports record Q3 memory revenue as AI demand grows

Posted Oct 30, 2026, 12:52 a.m. EDT

October 29, 2026

Samsung Electronics (005930.KS) reported approximately ₩195 trillion in Q3 2026 revenue and ₩107 trillion in operating profit. Memory revenue reached approximately ₩141 trillion. The figures were released before the external review was complete and remain subject to review adjustments.

Samsung attributed its memory performance to strong AI demand, higher market prices and a sales mix focused on AI products. HBM4 sales expanded, alongside demand for server SSDs. The company expects AI infrastructure investment to accelerate in 2027 and supply shortages to tighten. Its sales plans emphasize HBM, server DRAM and SSDs, including QLC storage for personal AI agents.

The company also confirmed a Q3 dividend of ₩4,601 per common or preferred share, scheduled for November 27, 2026, for holders on the September 30 record date. Its estimated ₩90–110 trillion shareholder-return programme was first announced in August. Samsung now expects ₩55–75 trillion remaining, including cash dividends and substantial share repurchases with cancellation. The final amount, execution plan and next shareholder-return policy are due at the late-January 2027 board meeting.

Sources: Samsung Q3 2026 results, Samsung Q3 earnings presentation, Samsung dividend disclosure, Samsung August shareholder-return announcement.

Anthropic opens a fuller view of AI platform economics

October 28, 2026

Anthropic's October 26 S-1 provides a detailed view of the company's model services, applications, customer growth and infrastructure commitments. The filing reports $16 billion of revenue for the first half of 2026. Its developer platform, coding tools and enterprise applications create several routes to paid usage.

Our research model values Anthropic at roughly $2 trillion at a Q4 2027 horizon, using about $199 billion of recognized sales over Q4 2027-Q3 2028 and a 10-times equity price-to-sales multiple. Continued rapid growth in paid usage is the largest driver of that estimate. Lower growth or a smaller sales multiple would materially reduce the valuation.

Cybersecurity offers a meaningful expansion route. Claude Security's current enterprise beta uses token billing, while critical-infrastructure and security partnerships broaden access to potential customers. Paid conversion after promotional credits and overlap with existing customers will determine the incremental revenue. Enterprise agents, professional workflows, life sciences, government, education and industrial applications create additional opportunities with distinct adoption and spending constraints.

The filing also details major compute and leased-capacity commitments, stock compensation, financing arrangements and public-benefit governance. These costs and claims make cash generation and capital access central to the investment case. The research includes scenarios in which slower demand and higher costs require substantial additional funding.

IPO pricing, final diluted shares and several contract details remain outstanding. Anthropic announced a $965 billion post-money preferred-financing valuation in May; future IPO terms will provide a new reference point.

Wazam: pricing duration and supplier costs shape the 2027 outlook

Posted Oct 27, 2026, 10:19 a.m. EDT

Wazam’s latest filed results show strong operating growth alongside substantial working-capital demands. The research model separately considers qualified low-loss material adoption, accepted manufacturing capacity and the conventional CCL price cycle.

A supplied UBS sector study dated 12 October 2026 forecasts conventional CCL pricing rising into mid-2027 and then fading. This is a broker scenario, not Wazam guidance. The model transfers only part of that selling-price change to an eligible portion of Wazam’s legacy output, while applying the full benchmark-implied incremental supplier-cost floor. It assigns the pricing event a 30% probability across macro states. The source’s July–August earnings observation overlaps the company results already used and creates no additional historical profit.

The resulting Q4 2027 model ceiling is about CNY230 per share, compared with about CNY225 before this review. It uses 20 times forecast forward-four-quarter attributable adjusted operating profit before financing and income tax, covering Q4 2027 through Q3 2028. This is a research estimate, not company guidance.

Customer qualification, usable capacity, supplier pricing, cash collection and funding remain important uncertainties. The direct new pricing and cost assumptions expire by Q2 2028; prior working-capital and financing effects can persist. Source coverage is limited to the supplied sector pages and available written records; the full sector report and complete spoken earnings calls were unavailable.

Palantir model update weighs growth against delivery costs

Posted Oct 26, 2026, 8:39 a.m. EDT

24 October 2026

Our Q4 2027 Palantir model ceiling rises from $68 to $81 per share, an increase of 19%. The calculation uses the existing 20x operating-profit multiple and includes stock compensation. Its earnings window runs from Q4 2027 through Q3 2028. This is our research estimate.

Palantir’s latest reported quarter remains Q2 2026, with revenue of $1,935 million and GAAP operating profit of $912 million. Management’s full-year revenue guidance is $8,150 million to $8,158 million. The next earnings release is scheduled for November 2.

The growth case depends on converting demand into paying deployments. We assign a 30% probability to our interpretation of management’s aspiration for broader-company growth to match the 149% growth rate reported by US commercial. Recent implementation, banking and sovereign-AI announcements strengthen the distribution case. Their undisclosed fees do not become extra revenue in the model. Reported contract value, remaining deal value and customer productivity gains also cannot be added together as separate sales.

Delivery economics remain central. The model retains hosting, engineering and support costs, research spending, stock compensation and dilution. The new $5,600 million cloud agreement replaces the prior schedule; it is not an additional commitment on top of it. The individual annual minimums have not been mapped publicly to specific years.

We also assign a 20% probability to a possible NHS contract break after the initial term ending in March 2027. No termination is confirmed. The model uses an assumed Palantir share of the consortium contract maximum, rather than treating the entire award as Palantir revenue.

ASTRA Research

Seagate (STX): Q4 2027 model forecast rises 2%

Posted Oct 22, 2026, 8:40 a.m. EDT
  • October 21, 2026 — Seagate (STX): +2% in our Q4 2027 modeled ceiling, from about USD 1,299 to USD 1,327 per share. New hard-drive pricing checks support higher earnings from a limited share of accepted storage capacity. These are conditional research estimates.

The opportunity comes from selling more storage capacity per drive through HAMR technology, alongside better prices on eligible orders. Precision manufacturing, customer qualification and longer production cycles limit how quickly additional capacity reaches buyers. Strong demand can therefore improve earnings faster than finished-drive output grows.

A Morgan Stanley preview dated October 20 describes some non-contracted nearline transactions at USD 40–70 per terabyte. Our model raises its existing conditional price endpoint from USD 30 to USD 40, keeping a 30% probability on 10% of qualified shipped storage capacity and a finite recognition period. After manufacturing, fulfillment and operating costs, the revision adds about USD 325 million of adjusted operating profit across Q4 2027 through Q3 2028.

The amount reaching Seagate remains uncertain. Customers have contracts with different renewal dates, and management described configuration and pricing commitments covering calendar 2027. Input costs, competitors' accepted capacity and customer bargaining power can also limit the benefit.

A separate, smaller Edge/IoT pricing allowance adds about USD 14 million of modeled adjusted operating profit through Q2 2027. It expires before the active valuation window. The existing valuation method and share basis are retained.

Seagate's October 27 results are the next checkpoint for accepted exabytes, manufacturer pricing, costs and updated guidance. The latest completed quarter ended July 3; the earnings call was July 28, while the issuer's release PDF carries a July 29 dateline.

Company sources: latest management earnings call, financial results and upcoming earnings event. The pricing observations are attributed broker research; the probabilities, earnings bridge and valuation are our estimates.

Factory timing, saleable output, acquisition recovery and funding remain the main uncertainties. This is a revision to our forecast assumptions.   • Amazon ($AMZN): our modeled value falls about 14% to $269 per share, from $314. AWS growth requires equipment, power, support and staff. Our revised forecast pays for that expansion and its depreciation, while treating sales of AI hardware as a different revenue stream with manufacturing costs. Some hardware sales replace cloud rentals already in the forecast. Conditional Globalstar operations include operating costs and possible dilution; their effect on this revision is small. Large future capital budgets require funding, a slower spending pace or stronger collections. Amazon second-quarter results, filed acquisition terms
  • Alphabet ($GOOGL): our modeled value falls about 13% to $363 per share, from $415. The forecast separates Cloud services from hardware transferred to customers, then pays the manufacturing, support and infrastructure costs of each. New AI software can improve returns, but its contribution depends on paid adoption after additional computing and support expense. Customer acceptance, competitive pricing and future funding remain uncertain. Alphabet second-quarter results

ASTRA Research

SpaceX raises the stakes for AI infrastructure

Posted Oct 21, 2026, 10:36 a.m. EDT

October 20, 2026

SpaceX reported about $15 billion of third-quarter revenue, including about $8 billion from its Superintelligence business. Management forecasts $33–37 billion of company revenue for the first quarter of 2027.

The biggest change is the pace of the proposed compute buildout. Management expressed high confidence in adding about 10 gigawatts during 2027, taking total capacity to about 13 gigawatts. Larger power plans still depend on construction, equipment, commissioning and financing.

Elon Musk also described a possible $500 billion–$1 trillion annualized revenue rate at the end of 2027 while discussing enterprise AI agents. That is an ambition rather than formal guidance. An annualized exit rate measures the pace reached near year-end; it does not mean the company collects that amount during 2027.

Our updated research model raises its Q4 2027 modeled value from about $100 to $296 per share, an increase of about 197%. It retains the same earnings multiple and includes depreciation, operating expenses and conditional share issuance. Delayed construction, the management capacity plan and a small-probability stretch outcome have separate revenue, cost and financing paths. These are research estimates, not company forecasts.

The distinction between cash generation and accounting earnings matters. Superintelligence produced about $5 billion of adjusted earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortization, while reported operating profit was about $400 million. Depreciation and employee share awards explain much of the difference. The company also expects $35–40 billion of capital spending in the fourth quarter. Further acquisition-accounting details remain pending.

For chip, memory, networking and power suppliers, the call supports a stronger demand outlook. Profit capture depends on qualified output, customer allocations, delivery dates and contract prices. Existing forecasts already assume substantial AI growth, so the same spending cannot be counted again for every supplier. SpaceX's internal turbine work also creates a competitive question for external power suppliers; it does not establish a canceled supplier order.

Sources: SpaceX Q3 results, investor relations and call replay.

Tobacco research: IQOS strength, Velo growth and Altria's replacement challenge

Posted Oct 21, 2026, 10:36 a.m. EDT

October 20, 2026

New research on Philip Morris, British American Tobacco and Altria highlights how differently the companies are replacing cigarette profits.

Philip Morris has the strongest established smoke-free business through IQOS. Higher revenue and gross profit per equivalent unit can improve its earnings mix. US ZYN faces tougher competition, while production and customer-acquisition costs absorb part of the growth. Our initial Q4 2027 model ceiling is $187 per share, using 15 times GAAP operating profit.

British American Tobacco offers a growing Velo business alongside its cigarette cash flow. Management aims for about £4 billion in modern-oral sales by 2030. Our initial ceiling is $75 per US ADS, using 10 times normalized operating profit after the Canadian settlement adjustment. Promotions, legal market access and the settlement burden remain material risks.

Altria must replace shrinking premium-cigarette and traditional-oral profit. Growing on! sales help, but retained pricing, manufacturing costs and promotion determine the contribution. NJOY's commercial return remains conditional. Our initial ceiling is $74 per share, using 10 times GAAP operating profit.

These are research estimates for the Q4 2027 valuation horizon, based on modeled profit from Q4 2027 through Q3 2028, rather than company price guidance. Philip Morris reports on October 21 and Altria on October 29; those upcoming results are not included.

Sources: Philip Morris second-quarter results, BAT September strategy update, Altria June financial filing.
